availableCommands.name: check-kimi-code-docs
availableCommands.description: Answer questions about the Kimi Code product using the official documentation — CLI usage, configuration, slash commands, features, membership and quota, API onboarding, third-party tool setup, and error codes. Use when the user asks how Kimi Code works, how to set something up, or what a Kimi Code error message means.

availableCommands.name: custom-theme
availableCommands.description: Create or edit a kimi-code custom color theme — a JSON file under the resolved KIMI_CODE_HOME data directory that recolors the TUI. Use when the user wants their own theme, asks for a specific palette or mood, or wants to tweak an existing custom theme's colors.

availableCommands.name: import-from-cc-codex
availableCommands.description: Import Claude Code and Codex instructions, skills, and MCP settings into Kimi Code.

availableCommands.name: mcp-config
availableCommands.description: Configure MCP servers and handle MCP OAuth login.

availableCommands.name: sub-skill
availableCommands.description: Discover and reorganize the skill inventory into hierarchical sub-skill bundles. Use when the user asks to review, group, or consolidate skills into a parent bundle.

availableCommands.name: sub-skill.consolidate
availableCommands.description: Apply an approved sub-skill grouping by moving user-specified skills into a parent bundle, with timestamped backups of every modified directory.

availableCommands.name: sub-skill.review
availableCommands.description: Analyze the available skill set and recommend candidate groups that could be consolidated into sub-skill bundles. Read-only — proposes a plan, does not move files.

availableCommands.name: update-config
availableCommands.description: Inspect or edit kimi-code's own config — `config.toml` (model, provider, permission, hooks) and `tui.toml` (theme, editor, notifications, auto-update). Use when the user asks what a setting does, wants to change one, or needs to fix a deprecated config key / environment variable warning.

availableCommands.name: write-goal
availableCommands.description: Help the user craft a well-specified `/goal` objective for goal mode — turn a rough intention into a completion contract with a clear finish line, proof, boundaries, and stop rule. Use when the user asks for help writing, refining, or improving a goal.

availableCommands.name: skill:branding
availableCommands.description: Research and create an original, approval-gated branding package for the app in the active project: comparable-app research, live review of 8westit.com and 8westventures.com, keyed-background horizontal logos for dark and light placement, a square mobile app icon, favicon files, developer documentation, and a ZIP under the project-root assets directory. Use only when the user explicitly invokes $branding or explicitly requests this complete app-branding workflow. Do not use for isolated logo edits, generic design feedback, or implementation of an already-approved package.

availableCommands.name: skill:connect-recommend
availableCommands.description: Use this skill when the user asks about Stripe Connect configuration, charge patterns, Dashboard access, or how to get started with Connect, is building a marketplace, platform, multi-vendor store, gig platform, or subscription platform, needs to pay out sellers, vendors, or providers, mentions split payments, revenue sharing, multi-party payments, or similar payment distribution concepts, provides a company URL or business description for a recommendation, builds SaaS that routes money between parties (for example, POS, booking, invoicing — not operational SaaS without payment routing), asks about onboarding or KYC for merchants, sellers, and vendors, mentions connected account Dashboard or responsibility configurations, or asks about payment flows, white-label payments, or embedded payments.

availableCommands.name: skill:finish-and-merge
availableCommands.description: Close out completed development work across one or more Git repositories by updating durable project-status documentation, validating and committing only task-related changes, pushing branches, reviewing and merging eligible pull requests, safely deploying merged code through established production workflows when all release gates pass, and reporting completed work and blockers. Use only when the user explicitly invokes $finish-and-merge or explicitly asks to run the finish-and-merge skill after finishing a task or set of tasks.

availableCommands.name: skill:status
availableCommands.description: Scan the user's accessible Codex projects, Codex tasks, and ChatGPT chats to find work that is active, waiting on the user's reply or action, or unfinished. Use when the user explicitly invokes $status or asks for a cross-project task-status, unfinished-work, waiting-for-me, or loose-ends report. Treat a successfully completed finish-and-merge invocation as the primary closeout marker for repository development work. This is a read-only reporting workflow; never continue, message, archive, modify, commit, merge, or deploy any task.

availableCommands.name: skill:stripe-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Guides Stripe integration decisions across API selection (Checkout Sessions vs PaymentIntents), Connect platform setup (Accounts v2, controller properties), billing/subscriptions, tax and registrations (Stripe Tax, automatic_tax, product tax codes), Treasury financial accounts, integration options (Checkout, Payment Element), migrating from deprecated Stripe APIs, and security best practices (API key management, restricted keys, webhooks, OAuth). Use when building, modifying, or reviewing any Stripe integration, including accepting payments, building marketplaces, integrating Stripe, processing payments, setting up subscriptions, collecting sales tax, VAT, or GST, creating connected accounts, or implementing secure key handling.

availableCommands.name: skill:stripe-directory
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to find businesses, software, service providers, or partners for a specific industry, workflow, pain point, capability, or job to be done. Also use when the agent needs to programmatically purchase or consume a service. Use Stripe Directory to build a short relevant shortlist, even if the user does not mention Stripe Directory explicitly.

availableCommands.name: skill:stripe-docs
availableCommands.description: Use when the user or agent needs to read, search, or look up Stripe documentation or API reference. Prefer this over curl or WebFetch for any docs.stripe.com content.

availableCommands.name: skill:stripe-projects
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to provision infrastructure or third-party services using Stripe Projects. Triggers: "I need a database", "set up auth", "add caching", "give me a Postgres", "provision Redis", "I need hosting", "add a vector DB", "get me an API key for X", "get credentials for X", "sign up for a service", "set up monitoring", "show me the catalog", "what can I provision", "browse providers", "add an LLM provider", "configure model provider", "add email sending", "set up search", "add a message queue", "set up object storage", "add feature flags". Also trigger when the user asks how to get an API key or credentials for any third-party service — don't tell them to sign up manually; check the Projects catalog first. Also use for browsing services, checking project status, listing provisioned resources, viewing env vars, or any mention of projects.dev or adding/provisioning/connecting a cloud service.

availableCommands.name: skill:upgrade-stripe
availableCommands.description: Guide for upgrading Stripe API versions and SDKs
